newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS-Indian shares, spurred by local buying, rally 6.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Indian shares, spurred by local buying, rally 6.0 pct.

text.p: Indian stock markets began the new year on a bullish note on Wednesday as a flurry of local buying saw blue-chip stocks soar on the back of an improved market sentiment, dealers said.

The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index surged 184.84 points, or 6.0 percent to 3,270.04, an intra-day high over its previous close. It closed at 175.86 points or 5.70 percent at a provisional 3,261.06.
The market rally was sparked by high expectations as a result of a government announcement on Tuesday proposing a series of policy measures to boost the country's capital markets, traders said.
"It's mainly a speculative bull run helped by a little bit of short-covering," said chief dealer Sanjeev Sanghvi at foreign brokerage James Capel B&K.
The government said it would announce policy measures this month to boost industrial growth and sagging markets.

"The government is likely to announce the decisions early January," H.K. Dua, information advisor to the prime minister, told reporters at the end of a five-hour meeting between industrialists and the Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

Market participants said the good news came at a time of depressed sentiment and widespread concern about the slowdown in the economy. Hit by the gloomy outlook, the Bombay stocks index fell to a three-year low of 2,713.12 in early December.

"Basically, the government has said it will take a broader look at the economy. This has given optimism for operators to pick up stocks," said institutional dealer, Ashish Wakankar at broking firm Sundar Iyer.

The topics discussed between the government officials and industrialists were revival of the capital market, credit availability, corporate taxation, delicensing and more opening of the economy, Dua said.
Expectations of increased fund allocation by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in Indian markets also led local players to build positions in frontline stocks.
"There is a little bit of anticipation of early FII allocations," said Capel's Sanghvi.
Dealers said speculators were active bidders in blue-chip stocks in anticipation of stepped-up buying by foreign funds, the major players in the market.
Many foreign institutions are closed on New Year's day.
"People are doing front-running..expecting foreign institutions to come into the market," said Vijay Pandya, chief dealer at Classic Share & Stock Brokers, a local firm.
"There are not many players around...we are seeing moderate volumes in the market."
